text.title: Fan-Out Retrieval Failure Modes
text.summary: Five ways a fan-out pays for retrieval more than once. All five are quiet: the pipeline produces correct output and the cost lands somewhere nobody is reading.

antipattern.description: Each subagent is briefed with a topic and told to look it up. Ten children, ten searches, one corpus.
antipattern.reason: The candidate set is re-sent to the provider by every fresh process, so the corpus scan is billed per child rather than per question. Measured at 22 calls in one pipeline for a handful of distinct questions. It hides well because each individual call looks cheap and none of them appear in the orchestrator's context.

antipattern.description: The orchestrator fetches a document, then inlines it into every child's brief so the children "do not have to fetch it".
antipattern.reason: Trades one cheap fetch per child for one expensive copy per child, then re-sends that copy on every turn of every child. The intuition is right — avoid the duplicate work — but the duplicate being avoided is the cheap one.

antipattern.description: Content is fetched without the sink flag and the body arrives on stdout, straight into the consuming context.
antipattern.reason: Loads the whole document unconditionally when the agent typically needs one section, and makes the cost proportional to document size rather than to what was used. The sink form is a flag away and returns a receipt of about 30 tokens.

antipattern.description: The pipeline reports agent-visible token counts and declares a win. The CLI's own provider calls are not in the report because they happened in child processes.
antipattern.reason: Produces confidently wrong conclusions: one measured run showed a small agent-visible reduction while being several times more expensive end to end. Any optimisation accepted on that evidence is unverified, and the regression it hides grows with fan-out width.

antipattern.description: Subagents are spawned without the subagent flag, so each injects whatever conversation context it can resolve.
antipattern.reason: Two costs for one omission. The transcript is paid on every child call, and because it is part of the cache key each child hashes differently and misses a shared cache entry a sibling has already warmed — turning a free repeat into a full-price search.
